card.title: The Winner’s Ceremony
card.instruction: Treat every contest, bargain, or decision as incomplete until the proper recognition, ritual, and consequence have occurred.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I won our coin toss. Please announce who sits by the window.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You do. Sit down; you're blocking the aisle.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then announce my name from your seat. I'll approach when called.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The conductor needs to get past us.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An official witness. Ask her to present the seat, and I'll accept it immediately.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 asks formal announcement, A3 waits to approach and A5 requires official presentation before taking the seat.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 practical seating request becomes A3 a named summons; B4 conductor obstruction becomes A5 an official witness.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 want the aisle clear and offer plausible urgency.

heightening.evidence: B4 obstruction is recruited into A5 the ritual that A says will permit immediate compliance.

specificity.evidence: A1 window-seat coin toss and B2 aisle blockage establish a train-seat allocation with immediate inconvenience.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 official witness uses B4 conductor specifically rather than inserting an unrelated ceremony.
